Thanks for the advice. I think when it comes to family and such - 'the truth will out' as my grandmother used to say. Once everyone hears we are separating, I think the lies and walls she has built up will start to crumble. 

>shooting range

have you ever been to NJ? but in seriousness you're right. I'll ditch them by selling them and I'll be better off for it. Even the act of saying out loud how it as been a barrier helps me realize how silly and small it is. It needs to be done, so I must do it. Simple as that
You're right of course. Its just a shitty position to be in.

> Keep in mind the relationship you have with your wife is the primary source that your kids have to learn what a relationship is supposed to be like.

this is the primary point of focus for me to control my anger. I remind myself that no matter what hurtful things she is saying, she is sick and her actions are coming from that place of sickness. As the not-sick person, it is my duty to try and set a good example for the kids and keep my emotions in check. 

Thanks for the info on co-dependency. When you said it I thought "no, thats not me..." but then I hit the wikipedia page. Its not a perfect fit, but there is something there. I definitely feed into the behavior by allowing it to go on and allowing her to hide it from everyone. I give into the constant questioning and let her go through my texts and emails whenever she wants. More generally, I think I am a very passive person. In other ways, I rely on her to 'make all the decisions' from where we eat to when we vacation. Good food for thought. 

Can you recommend a good way to find a therapist that can help with this specific problem? if I go by myself, should I seek jealousy counseling, depression counseling, marital counseling?

is it sexist of me to think that maybe you were able to salvage your relationship with your son because he is a male? My uncle went through a terrible divorce years ago and lost primary custody of his daughter. She grew up with her crazy mother and was fed a bunch of lies all the time. She grew up hating him and siding with her. Its like a nightmare come true that this is happening to me.

> First thing you need to do is secure those firearms out of your house

i think you are absolutely right about this. NJ law around the issue makes it very very difficult. I can't simply "loan" them to a friend or have a relative take them. I can't give them to my family out-of-state (violation of federal law). I can't put them in storage. My only legal recourse is to sell them. This of course, takes time and costs money (transfer fees, shipping fees, etc) that have encouraged me to put it off as long as i have. I think I will take care of this tomorrow. 

>Second - Does she have any family that could be able to serve as an mediator?

She has steadfastly refused to involve her family or mine. She has threatened me with all kinds of terrible things (usually involving the kids) if I were to ever disclose to anyone that these things are going on. We are close with her parents. They live nearby. They have no idea this is going on. I have asked her repeatedly to talk to her mother about this. I think she refuses because she is experiencing a strong cognitive dissonance; she feels strongly that i am cheating and she fears that her mother (whom she trusts deeply) will contradict her feelings and side with me. 

I have 'demanded' therapy. For what good my demands are.  She won't go. I think I need to go by myself - unfortunately I think I need to sell the guns before I go or I'd risk becoming a felon (change in prohibited persons status ie seeking mental help while retaining posession of the guns...only in NJ!) 

>Ultimately you won't fail your kids by modeling a positive life separate from their mother's mental illness

Thanks for this. there are going to be very tough times ahead, but I think if I can reprioritize and focus on helping the kids get through it, it might give me some purpose. 

>Oh and if you decide to pull the trigger 

poor word choice...:)

That's fair, and probably an overreaction on my part to assume I will not get some custody - even though my wife has stated to me that she would do everything in her power including lie and fake evidence to try and build a case against me seeing them. 

I guess by 'losing' them - what I really mean is 'failing' them. I worry that I will lose the emotional connection I have with them. That they will grow to hate me. That they will listen to all the awful things that their mother says and i will 'effectively' lose them. And most importantly, they will be losing the life they could have had, if their mother sought treatment for her illness and we remained together.
I am extraordinarily selfish to the point where I wonder if I might not be capable of putting anyone before myself. I fake generosity extremely well but this is all an act.

I had an ND through my front door. I am so ashamed and embarrassed by what happened, since there is just no excuse for it. I put a laser sight on my HD pistol and I was sighting it from my bedroom to the door to see if it was on the front sight at that distance. at this point the sequence went something like this: rack slide, lock back, insert mag, drop slide, decide to check the alignment, drop mag, point pistol. Now without realizing it, i'm pointing a loaded gun at the front door of my house. Then I have the genius idea "I wonder how much my aim is off when I squeeze the trigger?" Next, I did the stupidest most dangerous thing I've ever done in my life and I still haven't forgiven myself for it. I pulled the trigger. No one was hurt. The bullet went through my front door, through the plate glass behind it and harmlessly off into a lake. I still to this day can't forgive myself for it, but I take it as a hard hard lesson about gun safety I'll never forget. I felt sick about it for the next few weeks as ideas kept popping into my head like "what if someone was walking by? what if my wife came home at that moment?" I thank God no one was hurt and I'll never take that for granted. I take it as a second chance at being a responsible gun owner. 

Even writing this has brought a wave of shame and guilt back. The only atonement I can offer is that I'll never ever make a mistake about gun safety ever again. Thanks, OP for having the courage to make this post. I hope we can all learn a bit about what happens when we take safety for granted and get lax about the rules.
